value.title: Introduction to JavaScript
value.description: Build JavaScript confidence from syntax to practical UI interactions with short lessons, checkpoints, and assignment handoffs.
value.authorsLine: By Tejas Sharma and Aviral Tyagi
overviewParagraphs: Description - Begin your JavaScript career today with a steady, practical learning flow.
This course is built for students who want to move from the basics into real browser interactions without feeling lost.
Videos and assignments are mixed together so students can practice in the same flow instead of leaving the course context.
sessionNotes: Keep a small list of syntax patterns you want to remember after each lesson.
Use the assignment checkpoints as proof that the lesson actually landed.

lessons.title: Assignment 1. Variables Practice Sheet
lessons.summary: Write and test a short JavaScript sheet that covers variables, data types, and simple condition checks.
instructions: Create a small file with at least five variables using different data types.
Add two condition checks and log the outputs clearly.
Keep the file tidy enough that a mentor can review it quickly.

lessons.title: Assignment 2. DOM Mini Audit
lessons.summary: Inspect a small page, list its key DOM targets, and describe how you would attach interaction handlers.
instructions: Pick one page from HackLab or your own project.
List the selectors you would need for the primary actions.
Write short notes for the interactions you would wire first.

value.title: UI Systems and Visual Hierarchy
value.description: A visual design playlist on spacing, rhythm, and hierarchy with assignment checkpoints placed between the lessons.
overviewParagraphs: This playlist is focused on visual hierarchy, spacing, and interface clarity.
Students can use it to improve weak layouts without redesigning an entire screen from scratch.
sessionNotes: Compare before-and-after layouts to see hierarchy improvements more clearly.

lessons.title: Assignment 1. UI Hierarchy Breakdown
lessons.summary: Break down one weak interface and show how hierarchy, contrast, and spacing can be improved.
instructions: Capture one interface that feels visually flat.
Write three hierarchy problems you notice first.
Suggest one concrete layout or contrast fix for each problem.

value.title: Creative Build Workflows
value.description: Follow the way HackLab mentors break a build into smaller checkpoints so projects feel easier to finish and review.
value.authorsLine: By Tejas Sharma and HackLab Build Team
overviewParagraphs: This course shows how to split a project into checkpoints, reviews, and clear next steps.
It works well for students who start strong but lose momentum before the final polish stage.
sessionNotes: Keep milestone notes short so each checkpoint stays actionable.

lessons.title: Assignment 1. Milestone Board
lessons.summary: Create a milestone board for one active project with stages, review checkpoints, and one fallback plan.
instructions: List the project goal in one sentence.
Split the work into at least three milestones.
Add one review checkpoint and one fallback plan if the sprint slips.
